notes: Ohio business income deduction (modeled): the first $250,000 of business income (Schedule C net profit) is deducted, and business income above $250,000 is taxed at a flat 3%, outside the regular brackets. For most freelancers this means no Ohio income tax on self-employment profit.

2026 nonbusiness schedule under R.C. 5747.02(A)(3)(c) as amended by H.B. 96: $0 on Ohio taxable nonbusiness income up to $26,050; above $26,050 the tax is $332 plus 2.75% of the excess (modeled). Business income is handled by the business income deduction above.

Discrepancy flag: the Ohio Department of Taxation's 2026 IT 1040ES worksheet still prints the 2025-style schedule ($342 + 2.75% to $100,000; 3.125% above). The flat 2.75% for 2026 is taken from the statute/H.B. 96; ODT's final 2026 IT 1040 instructions were not available on 2026-10-22 and should be checked.

Personal exemption depends on modified AGI (indexing suspended for 2025-2026 by H.B. 96): $2,400 (MAGI <= $40,000), $2,150 ($40,001-$80,000), $1,900 ($80,001 up to the cap), $0 at MAGI of $500,000 or more for 2026. $1,900 per taxpayer/spouse is used here; dependents not modeled.

Credits not modeled: joint filer credit, $20 exemption credit, nonrefundable credits based on MAGI, retirement/senior credits, earned income credit, credit for taxes paid to other states, and Ohio's own self-employed health insurance/medical deduction rules (Ohio Schedule of Adjustments line 44).

seDeduction.note: Ohio starts from federal AGI, which already reflects the deductible half of SE tax (it reduces nonbusiness income because business income is measured from Schedule C net profit).

seHealthInsurance.note: Inherited through federal AGI; Ohio's separate unreimbursed health-care deduction must be reduced by the federal SE health insurance deduction to avoid double counting.

retirementContributions.note: SEP/solo 401(k) deductions in federal AGI flow through; no Ohio add-back.

qbi.note: The federal QBI deduction is not in Ohio's federal-AGI starting point; Ohio instead has its own $250,000 business income deduction and 3% flat rate (see notes).

localIncomeTax.note: Most Ohio cities and villages levy a municipal income tax (commonly about 1%-2.5%, some higher) on wages and on net profits of self-employed residents and businesses operating there, filed with the city or a collection agency (RITA/CCA). Many school districts also levy a school district income tax (SD 100) on residents: 'traditional base' districts tax Ohio taxable income, 'earned income base' districts tax wages and self-employment income. Rates and coverage vary by address, so neither is modeled.

localities.name: Columbus
localities.note: Columbus taxes residents' wages and net profits at 2.50% and gives a 100% credit (up to 2.50%) for tax paid to the city where you work. School district income taxes are not included.

estimatedTax.threshold: Estimated Ohio tax liability (total tax minus credits) less Ohio withholding of more than $500
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Required installments are based on the lesser of 90% of the 2026 Ohio tax or 100% of the 2025 Ohio tax (IT 1040ES worksheet lines 9-11); interest penalty computed on IT/SD 2210. School district tax estimates are separate (SD 100ES).
estimatedTax.form: IT 1040ES worksheet; pay with the Ohio Universal Payment Coupon (OUPC) for 2026

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $99 Articles of Organization (Ohio Secretary of State Form 610).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: None - Ohio does not require LLC annual reports.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: None (Ohio's corporate franchise tax was replaced by the CAT).
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: Commercial Activity Tax (CAT) applies only to Ohio taxable gross receipts above $6,000,000 per year (tax years 2025 onward) at 0.26%; businesses below $6 million do not file or pay. Not relevant to a typical freelancer.
